reading.body:
QTS Aurora-Denver 1 occupies a 65-acre owned campus in Arapahoe County with stated critical power capacity of 160 MW or greater. The operator's own language distinguishes this as planned or build-out capacity rather than confirmed current operating capacity, so the actual power available for IT load today is not published. If the full 160 MW reaches operating status, assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, the campus could host roughly 4,000 racks. No per-building square footage, cooling redundancy, or tenant information is published.

Within Colorado, QTS Aurora-Denver 1 ranks fourth by published megawatts among facilities whose operators have stated a figure. The state has 17 mapped data center facilities total, but only three publish capacity numbers. Colorado's three published facilities total 26.35 MW, meaning this single campus would more than quintuple that total if its 160 MW capacity reaches operating status. The scale difference between published and potential capacity here reflects the gap between existing regional AI infrastructure and committed expansions.

This campus sits within a multi-region QTS footprint spanning Texas, Arizona, Ohio, New Jersey, Illinois, and Colorado. QTS itself is owned by Blackstone and was acquired as a mature operator with established facilities across North America. Whether the Aurora campus functions as regional compute capacity for AI workloads, cloud services, or other uses is not specified in the published facts.
